# This file

This report investigates changes in hippocampal and amygdala volume following
an eight-week bright-light therapy study. Participants were randomly assigned
to a control group or a bright-light group. MRI measurements were collected
before and after the intervention.

# Descriptive statistics

The original sample consisted of 80 participants, with 40 in each group.
Three participants had missing post-treatment hippocampal volume measurements. One individual had unrealistically high hippocampal measurements, and was thus excluded.
After cleaning, 76 participants remained, with 38 participants in each group.

<!-- Information source: scripts/clean_data.py and scripts/descriptive_stats.py -->

## What is the age distribution by group?

The mean age was 26.8 years in the control group and 28.2 years in the
bright-light group.

![](figures/age_distribution.png)

## What is the sex distribution by group?

The control group included 20 females and 18 males. The bright-light group
included 19 females and 19 males.

![](figures/sex_distribution.png)

## Does the country of origin differ between the groups?

The control group included 24 participants from Australia and 14 from Sweden.
The bright-light group included 16 participants from Australia and 22 from
Sweden. The country distribution therefore differed between the groups. This difference may be relevant when interpreting the results. However, the
difference alone does not establish that country is a confounding factor.

![](figures/country_distribution.png)

# Hippocampal volume

## Does hippocampal volume change from baseline to post-treatment?

A paired t-test compared hippocampal volume before and after the intervention
in the same participants.

<!-- Results source: scripts/t_tests.py -->

The change was statistically significant
(*t* = 3.55, *p* < .001), indicating that hippocampal volume changed
on average across the participants.

<!-- Figure source: figures/hippocampal_baseline_post.png -->

![](figures/hippocampal_baseline_post.png)

## Does this change differ between the control and bright-light groups?

A Welch's independent t-test compared the change scores between groups.

<!-- Results source: scripts/t_tests.py -->

The difference between groups was not statistically significant
(*t* = -0.90, *p* = .374). There was insufficient evidence that hippocampal
volume change differed between the control and bright-light groups.

<!-- Figure source: figures/hippocampal_change_by_group.png -->

![](figures/hippocampal_change_by_group.png)

# Amygdala volume

## Does amygdala volume change from baseline to post-treatment?

A paired t-test compared amygdala volume before and after the intervention
in the same participants.

<!-- Results source: scripts/t_tests.py -->

The change was statistically significant
(*t* = 4.05, *p* < .001), indicating that amygdala volume changed
on average across the participants.

<!-- Figure source: figures/amygdala_baseline_post.png -->

![](figures/amygdala_baseline_post.png)

## Does this change differ between the control and bright-light groups?

A Welch's independent t-test compared amygdala volume change between groups.

<!-- Results source: scripts/t_tests.py -->

The difference between groups was not statistically significant
(*t* = -1.29, *p* = .203). There was insufficient evidence that amygdala
volume change differed between the control and bright-light groups.

<!-- Figure source: figures/amygdala_change_by_group.png -->

![](figures/amygdala_change_by_group.png)

# Relationship between hippocampal and amygdala volume changes

## Are changes in hippocampal volume associated with changes in amygdala volume?

A Pearson correlation examined the relationship between the changes in the
two brain regions.

<!-- Results source: scripts/correlation.py -->

The correlation was weak and positive (*r* = .158, *p* = .172).
The association was not statistically significant, so there was insufficient
evidence of a linear relationship between changes in the two brain regions.

<!-- Figure source: figures/brain_volume_correlation_by_group.png -->

![](figures/brain_volume_correlation_by_group.png)

# Conclusion

Hippocampal and amygdala volumes changed significantly from baseline to post-treatment 
when participants were considered together. However, neither region showed a significant difference 
in volume change between the control and bright-light groups.

The correlation between changes in the two brain regions was weak and not statistically significant. 
Overall, there was insufficient evidence that bright-light therapy produced different changes in 
brain volume compared with the control condition.
